clue.text: Beach god finds girl

parts.note: a beach is made of sand
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A deity turns up on the shore and meets a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a girl's given name, so it stands for a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Rising pop celebrity upset old primate

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: pa, like pop, is an informal word for father

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down answer these letters run backwards

parts.note: a name is a celebrity, as in a big name

explanation.surface: An ageing pop star, now distressed, is likened to an old ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Apeman refers to an early hominid, a primitive primate between ape and human.

clue.text: Southern pirate in exploit that's illustrated

indicators.note: in places the pirate's pieces inside the exploit

parts.note: a deed is a heroic act or exploit
to crib is to copy illicitly, to pirate

explanation.surface: A buccaneer from the south features in an adventure story with pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to depict or portray it, so illustrated can mean described.

clue.text: Inconstant peri had to love goddess

indicators.note: inconstant means changeable, so the letters of these words shift about

explanation.surface: A fickle fairy had to fall for a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy of Persian myth. 'love' looks like a verb but belongs with 'goddess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Chief old and small for example heading West

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means travelling right to left, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: minor means small or lesser

explanation.surface: A tribal leader, elderly and slight, sets an example by riding into the sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was an Apache leader, a chief of his people.

clue.text: Giant pig about to carry dog around

indicators.note: to carry is to hold within, so the dog piece goes inside the pig piece
about means turned round, so the word for pig is read backwards

parts.note: a hog is a pig

indicators.note: around means turned the other way, so the word for dog is reversed

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: An enormous pig circles round, carrying a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal but is a verb, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant Philistine slain by David.

clue.text: Tory supporters absolutely correct in opinion

definitions.meaning: the political ..., conservatives as a group
... meaning completely, as in ... to the end
being in the ..., correct in one's view

explanation.surface: Conservative backers are utterly convinced their views are correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Right covers the political conservatives, an intensifier meaning completely, and being correct.

clue.text: Hinge needs repair — that's Arab's comment!

indicators.note: something that needs repair is broken, so the letters of hinge are reordered

explanation.surface: A man from Arabia remarks that a hinge is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: An Arab is also a breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the sound a horse makes, and an Arab is a horse breed.

clue.text: Independent state positively in small man's grip

indicators.note: in signals that one piece goes inside the other
a grip holds something within, so the man's name encloses the other letters

parts.note: Mick is a shortened form of the man's name Michael
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A free agent says things confidently while a little man clutches him.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an unorthodox, independent-minded person who goes their own way.

clue.text: Astronomer runs little school sending rotter outside

indicators.note: the rotter is sent round the outside of the other letters, enclosing them
the rotter is sent round the outside of the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible person, a rotter
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
Sch is a short form, a little version, of the word school

explanation.surface: A stargazer manages a small school and expels a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: William Herschel discovered Uranus; he and his sister Caroline were noted astronomers.

clue.text: Mourn first woman on collapsed rig

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it
a collapsed structure has its parts jumbled, so the letters of rig are rearranged

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Grieving over a woman who was the first on an oil rig that fell down.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is to feel or express sorrow for a loss, i.e. to mourn.

clue.text: Spanish district where one may drink port

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port, often just Rio

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood in Spain where you can enjoy a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrio is a district or quarter of a Spanish-speaking town.

clue.text: Lunatic another to box current champion booed

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the other letters take the next one inside
lunatic means crazy, so the letters of another go wild

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A madman squares up to a booed boxing champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to box' puts I inside ANTHERO, the anagram of ANOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central figure lacking heroic virtues, a protagonist the audience may jeer.

clue.text: Popular name for pub

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A well-liked name for a public house.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, a place serving drink and often lodging.

clue.text: British PC having to face the music — that's novel!

parts.note: right-on means politically correct
rock is a genre of music

explanation.surface: A British police constable has to answer for his conduct, which is quite a story.
explanation.walkthrough: PC suggests a police constable but means politically correct. Brighton Rock is Graham Greene's 1938 novel, named after the hard seaside sweet stick sold in the English resort of Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is a celebrated novel by Graham Greene.

clue.text: January not starting pleasant — in danger of soaking?

indicators.note: not starting means losing the opening letter, applied to both the month word and the pleasant word

parts.note: January is a month
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Early in the new year the weather turns pleasant, though there may be a risk of a drenching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' governs both January's word and pleasant's word; the word 'in' does double duty, supplying its letters and starting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating on thin ice risks falling through into the water, a soaking; the idiom means at risk.

clue.text: Vehicle providing last trip in colour went through

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the colour

parts.note: red is a colour
a hearse carries the dead on their final journey

explanation.surface: A vehicle offering one final ride, painted in colour, drove through.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise, to go through a performance beforehand.

clue.text: One elder to wander all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person drifts off and wanders everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' suggests an older person; it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Danewort is the dwarf elder, a species of the elder plant genus Sambucus.

clue.text: Sewing initially confuses little one — could it be this?

definitions.text: Sewing initially confuses little one — could it be this?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word sewing

parts.note: to addle is to muddle or confuse
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A child finds needlework bewildering: could this particular stitch be the reason?
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is British informal for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddle stitch is a kind of sewing, a running stitch used in leatherwork and bookbinding.

clue.text: Some colliers are buried

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is a portion of the word

explanation.surface: Some miners lie buried underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The dead lie in their graves, which means they are buried there.

clue.text: Die long time after Durbeyfield girl

indicators.note: after places the long-time piece behind the girl's name

parts.note: Tess Durbeyfield is the heroine of Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A long time passes after Hardy's heroine dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' looks like a verb but is the noun: a small cube.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera was a small cube, in ancient use a die for games or a mosaic piece.

clue.text: On strike — then work to escape

parts.note: workers out are on strike
to run a machine is to work or operate it

explanation.surface: Workers walk out and then work again in order to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun pursuers is to escape them by being faster.

clue.text: Bottle good as weapon

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: A bottle is good enough to use as a weapon in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical agent used in warfare, a weapon of mass destruction.

clue.text: Mercenary having dined heartily tucked into meat

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the heart goes inside the meat

parts.note: veal is meat from a calf

indicators.note: heartily here means from the heart, so take the central letter of the word dined

explanation.surface: A greedy hired soldier ate well, tucking into some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating but puts N, the heart of 'dined', inside VEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means open to bribery, motivated by money, like a mercenary.

clue.text: Do well in grand public school

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
Eton is the famous English public school, meaning private and fee-paying

explanation.surface: Thrive at a prestigious private school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a fee-paying private school, Eton the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on is to make progress or succeed in life.

clue.text: Sun exposed this high-flier's failings

parts.note: reads like a tabloid exposé of a celebrity; really the mythical youth whose wax wings melted when he flew too near the sun

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper revealed a high-flying celebrity's flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but here it is the sun in the sky, which melted the wax of the flier's wings so they failed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too close to the sun, which melted his waxen wings and he fell.

clue.text: Saint using web to find poem

parts.note: on, as in being on a drug, means using it
a net is a web of mesh

explanation.surface: A holy man goes online to look for some verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem, as written by Shakespeare and Petrarch.

clue.text: Agent in misery as wounded

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy lies in pain, hurt and miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a representative sent on a mission, an agent of another.

clue.text: Olympics venue welcomes a legendary runner

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics

explanation.surface: An Olympic host city greets a famous athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek myth, beaten in a footrace by golden apples.

clue.text: Close friend in Grenadier Guards

indicators.note: to guard is to hold within, so the answer is kept inside these words

explanation.surface: An intimate pal serving in the Grenadier Guards regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close friend' looks like one phrase, but 'Close' is the definition. The Grenadier Guards are a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A close is a conclusion, the end of something, as in the close of play.
